metadata.boundary: Byte-identity holds only under json.dumps(indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) plus a trailing newline; the other five dump settings probed all diverge, so a naive re-dump is not byte-identical. Measured on ONE epoch-1 population at schema_version 1.19 whose key order was already sorted everywhere and which carried zero duplicate keys and zero embedded newlines. A state exhibiting any of those three is outside the measured envelope, as is any schema_version beyond 1.19.

environment.population: the live epoch-1 .ea/state.json: 5,743,039 bytes across 15 collections and 10,684 JSON objects, including 1,284 wave rows and 849 actual rows

limits.basis: P6 per-collection byte census; waves is the dominant collection
limits.name: largest_collection_share

limits.basis: P5 numbers census over 5847 float values
limits.name: float_roundtrip_failures

limits.basis: P5 non_ascii_strings census; an importer must survive at least this many
limits.name: non_ascii_strings_to_handle

metadata.surface: epoch-1 state.json population that the epoch-2 importer must consume

metadata.boundary: Measured from --version, --help and config-inspection paths only, with zero billed generation, so every finding is about what the CLI ADVERTISES rather than what it does when driven. Capability rows carrying no probe rule (skills, plan_mode, sub_agents, cache_control, error_class_surface) are declared-only and were not measured at all. opencode was absent from PATH, so all eight of its rows are unmeasured rather than passing. Versions are a point-in-time reading of one workstation's installs.

environment.population: 3 declared runtimes x 8 capability rows = 24 conformance rows; 16 probed against two installed binaries and 8 unmeasured

limits.basis: drift.json installed flag across the three declared runtimes
limits.name: runtimes_installed

limits.basis: drift.json DRIFT rows: session_resume on claude-code and on codex
limits.name: declared_vs_observed_drift

limits.basis: drift.json MISSING rows: all eight opencode rows, binary absent from PATH
limits.name: unmeasured_capability_rows

metadata.surface: installed provider runtime CLI capability surface (claude, codex, opencode)

metadata.boundary: Write concurrency was measured only in an isolated scratch workspace with its own socket path and its own daemon; the live daemon's write path was never contended, so the portalock ceiling is a scratch-workspace number. Head-of-line blocking was measured against a synthetic SYNCHRONOUS handler (1 ping completed during a 1 s sync hold versus 134 during an async hold of the same length) - a mixed sync/async handler set is outside the envelope. Every latency figure comes from one workstation against one 5.7 MB state file.

environment.population: 2,540 read RPCs across concurrency 1 to 64, plus 40 portalocker writers across concurrency 2 to 16, against one live daemon and one isolated scratch daemon

limits.basis: read_ladder daemon.ping at c64: 1280 calls, 0 errors, p95 5.32 ms
limits.name: ping_concurrency

limits.basis: read_ladder state.read p95 507.25 ms at c4 versus 84.41 ms at c1, a 6x knee
limits.name: state_read_concurrency

limits.basis: portalock ladder: 0 errors through c8, then 2/12 at c12 and 6/16 at c16
limits.name: portalock_writer_concurrency

limits.basis: worst read_ladder daemon.ping p95, measured at c64
limits.name: ping_p95_ms

metadata.surface: eawf daemon JSON-RPC under concurrent readers and the portalocker write fallback

metadata.boundary: Measured over the production corpus -- this project's own live epoch-1 .ea tree at cutover, 4,638 rows in the thousands band -- plus nine committed corpora that cover the structural shapes the live one does not exhibit. Ten corpora is the whole measured population: a corpus shape outside that set is unmeasured, not passing. The four legs are dry run, apply, idempotent rerun and rollback over a tree that declared itself disposable, so nothing here characterises an apply against a tree in use, a concurrent apply, or a corpus in the tens-of-thousands band. Two of the ten corpora are refusals rather than imports, and what is measured about them is that the refusal repeats identically and leaves the target byte-identical -- not that the importer handles their content.

environment.population: the live epoch-1 corpus at cutover: 4,638 rows, a thousands corpus magnitude, rehearsed alongside nine committed corpora covering the empty, terminal, multi-root, interrupted, attention-bearing, historical and refused shapes

limits.basis: row census of the live epoch-1 corpus staged at cutover; the thousands band holds from this count up to the next order of magnitude
limits.name: corpus_rows

limits.basis: published epoch-2 generation over staged epoch-1 corpus bytes; observed 1.319 against a declared ceiling of 1.60
limits.name: generation_multiplier

limits.basis: one apply over the live corpus; observed 3.849 s against a 30 s budget
limits.name: apply_wall_clock_s

limits.basis: the generation's own document after the terminal records move to their ledgers; observed 396,720 B against a 1.6 MB bound
limits.name: residual_document_bytes

metadata.surface: the epoch-2 importer run end to end over this project's own live epoch-1 corpus, at the scale the cutover actually has to survive

intent.desired_outcome: The fallback close arms the gate identically to the daemon path and P30-I24's criteria are drained
planned_steps: Pass the verify block ODR dials into the fallback close_iter call under P32-I01-W34|Drain P30-I24 with eawf spec convert-legacy
intent.problem: The iter-close ODR gate is enforced on the daemon path and silently advisory on the portalocker fallback path

B108.resolution: The CLI iter-close fallback threads odr_floor and odr_blocking from the verify block; the I24 drain is moot because legacy is a sanctioned criterion kind (closeout audit A-P33-CLOSEOUT)
B108.title: Arm the ODR gate on the iter-close fallback path and drain I24

B109.description: Claude writes its turn_duration row only when a turn ENDS so a wave claimed mid-turn baselines at the pre-turn total and banks the entire turn including the part before it existed. W43-W45 show it live: claimed against a zero baseline they took all 34.7 minutes of a turn that began 12 minutes earlier. Bounded by one turn but turns run 34-94 minutes while these waves measure 6-40 so it can exceed the measured quantity. Attribute a turn to the waves active during it.
B109.resolution: W33 pro-rates a turn straddling a claim by event timestamps (MEASURE_VERSION 8) (evaluation audit A-P34-I01-EVAL)
B109.title: Stop a wave claimed mid-turn from banking the whole turn

B110.description: The claim path (_capture_runtime_baseline in workflow/lifecycle/wave.py) is the one runtime-snapshot writer that does not record shared_wave_count so a baseline carries null and the divisor is recovered from the latest snapshot alone. Harmless today because shared_wave_divisor takes the max across both snapshots but P30-I25-W46 CR-01 asks that a snapshot record the concurrency it was captured under and this one does not. The daemon claim path knows the active-wave count; thread it through.
B110.resolution: P33-I01-W67 stamps shared_wave_count on the claim-time runtime baseline (closeout audit A-P33-CLOSEOUT)
B110.title: Stamp the concurrent-wave count on the claim-time baseline

B111.description: W51 excludes an interrupted turn by recognising the row Claude writes immediately before the closeout: system/agents_killed or an interruption marker. The rule is exact on the 330 transcripts here but depends on undocumented row shapes. If a release renames the marker the exclusion stops working silently and the wall-clock figure returns as an INCREASE which nothing catches. Pin the marker contract and add a scan that fails when an unmarked turn outruns every turn ever observed.
B111.resolution: W33 pins the interrupt marker against a recorded transcript fixture (evaluation audit A-P34-I01-EVAL)
B111.title: Detect a regression in the interrupt-marker contract

B112.description: W02 CR-04 asked for a per-wave in-flight guard spanning claim through dispatch through persist. What shipped is a post-hoc terminal re-read under the state lock which drops an attempt landing after close but does not prevent a dispatch racing a close-on-behalf during the unlocked spawn. The wave outcome records the deferral; this row records it in state.
B112.title: Guard the dispatch in-flight window across the unlocked spawn

B113.description: W06 CR-05 pins the four lifecycle invariants with tests/e2e/test_lifecycle_consistency.py, whose live drive is skipped unless EAWF_LIVE_E2E is set. The default-run assertions exercise in-memory helper logic rather than the daemon, so in CI the invariants are attested by the paid drive alone. A stubbed-adapter driver through fleet plus state.mutate would make CR-01 through CR-04 falsifiable on every run.
B113.title: Give the cross-runtime lifecycle invariants a spawn-free driver

B114.description: P30-I25-W41 is CLOSED with an outcome but carries no Wave.commit and has no matching wave-prefixed commit on the branch: its two deliverables landed under sibling wave commits (cd31b63d, ff6a6a8f). The work is present; the provenance is not derivable by git log --grep, which is how wave_sha resolves an unpinned wave. Pin the SHA or record the absorption.
B114.resolution: Abandoned in the v0.7 proposal: names a verb or record the epoch-2 cutover deletes, so no substance survives the rename.
B114.title: Reconcile the P30-I25-W41 commit-less ledger row

B115.description: roadmap revise --add-wave --success takes a comma-separated list with no escape, so any criterion whose prose contains a comma is silently split into fragments. P30-I21-W36 and P30-I25-W53 landed rows reading 'its bullets' and 'bucketed'. The flag fragments exactly the criteria the typed-criteria floor exists to protect, and a closed wave cannot be resynced. Take repeatable --success or a spec file, and reject a fragment under the 20-char floor rather than converting it.
B115.resolution: P33-I01-W15 made --success repeatable and rejects a fragment under the 20-char floor (closeout audit A-P33-CLOSEOUT)
B115.title: Stop --success splitting a criterion on its own commas

B116.description: The round writer pairs claims to open questions by index order (zip over the written claims and the OPEN questions), so a round's Nth claim marks the Nth OPEN question ANSWERED whether or not it answers it. The link is written both ways and the lifecycle is correct; only the pairing is a heuristic. Replace it with a semantic link, or narrow the auto-resolve to the single-open-question case where index order cannot be wrong.
B116.resolution: W32 auto-answers a question only when a claim pairs with a single open candidate (evaluation audit A-P34-I01-EVAL)
B116.title: Pair a claim to the question it actually answers

B117.description: tools/commit_prefix_lint.py validates the shape of a wave id in a commit subject but never checks that the wave exists in state.json. A commit can therefore attribute itself to a wave nobody planned, which is a phantom row in the ledger that git log --grep resolves and state.json does not. The lint has state.json available; it should reject an id that names no wave.
B117.resolution: The commit lint rejects a prefix naming a wave absent from state, with bidirectional edge checks.
B117.title: Reject a commit prefix naming a wave that does not exist

B118.description: The zero-EU close gate has one call site: the daemon state.mutate handler. The in-process close (used under EAWF_DAEMONLESS, and on a transport-fallback when the daemon RPC fails) runs the deterministic and verdict gates but never the zero-runtime check, so it closes a wave with elapsed_eu=0.0 behind a stderr advisory. Same class as the band-narrowed gate W52 was written to close: a gate that does not fire on every path is not a gate.
B118.resolution: P33-I01-W10 runs the zero-runtime close gate on the in-process close path (closeout audit A-P33-CLOSEOUT)
B118.title: Enforce the zero-runtime close gate on the in-process close path

B119.description: Spend accrues only when a lane finishes, and the cap is tested at the claim gate and between finished lanes, so an in-flight lane is never measured against it. One lane that burns 200 USD over hours under a 5 USD cap is never killed: the run records the overshoot, then stops claiming. hard_halt reaps the other lanes, never the one that blew the cap. Probe in-flight spend with a per-lane deadline, or rename the caps as claim gates -- the arm modal presents usd_cap as a spend cap.
B119.resolution: P33-I01-W25 relabels the fleet caps as claim gates in the arm modal; the in-flight spend kill is the native W67 Run meter (closeout audit A-P33-CLOSEOUT)
B119.title: Make the fleet spend cap bound spend, not just claims

B120.description: Two defects that likely stop the jail launching on Linux; unverified, the dev host is macOS. env_scrub pins TMPDIR to /private/tmp unconditionally, a macOS-only path, and Node (the claude CLI) returns it verbatim, so a Linux spawn hits ENOENT on its first temp write. jail.py also emits --tmpfs for every credential-deny entry, including .npmrc which is a FILE and ~/.aws which usually does not exist: bwrap fails ENOTDIR on a file and EROFS on an absent path, exiting before the agent starts.
B120.resolution: Linux sandbox TMPDIR pin and bubblewrap mask fix delivered by P31-W16 and gated by the linux-jail CI job running real bwrap.
B120.title: Fix the Linux sandbox: TMPDIR pin and the bwrap tmpfs masks

B121.description: command_exit_zero runs subprocess.run(argv) with the daemon's full environment and no argv validation. Two of three producers validate at construction, but the /audit skill builds the CheckSpec straight from its criterion_checks arg, which is free-form agent-supplied input -- so a crafted argv runs with AWS, GH_TOKEN and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the child env. This phase moved these gates onto the live close path. Call validate_gate_argv in the builder and use build_child_env.
B121.resolution: command_exit_zero validates its argv through validate_gate_argv and builds its env with build_child_env (closeout audit A-P33-CLOSEOUT)
B121.title: Validate the argv of an audit-DSL command gate and scrub its env

B122.description: start_egress_proxy, egress_socket_env and classify_egress have zero production callers, while the macOS seatbelt profile explicitly emits allow network and allow system-socket, so a jailed agent has unrestricted outbound. The jail's own comment defers this to P31 honestly, but the dispatch runner still describes the sandbox boundary as including an egress proxy. Either wire it or correct the module prose that implies it is live.
B122.resolution: P33-I01-W25: the sandbox jail and env scrub state that outbound traffic is unrestricted instead of implying an enforced egress proxy (closeout audit A-P33-CLOSEOUT)
B122.title: Wire the egress proxy or stop implying it is enforced

B123.description: Local-only trades away cross-machine continuity: a clone starts with an empty Feed and no telemetry history. Restore it explicitly rather than by tracking the firehose. export bundles the machine-local artifacts (event store, telemetry db, spec cache, .ea/local drafts) into an archive; import merges them back, deduplicating append-only stores by envelope id and refusing to clobber state.json. The archive carries absolute paths and raw agent output, so it is private by construction.
B123.title: Add eawf export and import for the local-only artifacts

B124.description: P30-I26-W06 raised the doctor byte cap to 64 KiB (interim) so doctor is not red on the ~52 KiB default AGENTS.md. Verify Codex's actual global+project truncation limit and trim AGENTS.md (or re-tighten the cap) so the guidance tail is not silently dropped for Codex users.
B124.resolution: The Codex project-doc cap is the measured 32768 bytes and AGENTS.md sits within it.
B124.title: Verify Codex's real project-doc cap and trim AGENTS.md

B125.resolution: W24 emits only the handler-backed session_end hook from the claude packager and guards codex hooks at import (evaluation audit A-P34-I01-EVAL)

B127.description: P30-I26-W03 relabelled the TUI steer control but two out-of-scope docstrings (kernel/state/models.py steer_notes, kernel/store/kinds/research_round.py) still claim notes shaped the round dispatch set, and the b-broadcast channel makes the same never-reaches-a-running-round claim. B127.title: Relabel the remaining research-steer honesty gaps

B128.description: P30-I26-W06 raised the doctor byte cap to 64 KiB (interim) so doctor is not red on the ~52 KiB default AGENTS.md. Verify Codex's actual global+project truncation limit and trim AGENTS.md (or re-tighten the cap) so the guidance tail is not silently dropped for Codex users.

B130.description: P30-I26-W14 got a 24.7 percent snapshot-suite drop tests-only. Residual ~110s is production check_affordance_parity per-key presses. Mirror the W12 sweep migration (classify UNRESOLVED via active_bindings) to pass the 40 percent target.

B131.description: P30-I26-W03 relabelled the TUI steer control, but kernel/state/models.py steer_notes + kernel/store/kinds/research_round.py docstrings still claim notes shaped the round dispatch set, and the b-broadcast channel makes the same never-reaches-a-running-round claim. B132.description: enable_profile validates against KNOWN_PROFILES, which _build_known_profiles derives from list_profiles() without a workspace argument - builtin bundle only. A new-id profile under .ea/profiles/ is discoverable by the loader union but cannot be enabled via the CLI. Pass the workspace root through the enable path so overlay ids resolve.
B132.resolution: W34 resolves workspace overlay profiles in profile enable and doctor (evaluation audit A-P34-I01-EVAL)
B132.title: config profile enable rejects workspace-overlay profile ids

B133.description: sync composes via load_profile(p) with no workspace argument (sync.py ~line 278; known-ids check ~line 222 likewise), so .ea/profiles/ overlay render_blocks never reach AGENTS.md and a same-id overlay cannot override builtin render content. Thread the target workspace into list_profiles/load_profile in the sync path.
B133.resolution: Sync passes the workspace through so profile overlays are selected; delivered by the v0.6.5 hotfix.
B133.title: eawf sync ignores workspace profile overlays when composing

B134.description: Phase audit F3: W08, W13, W20, W26 and W41-W46 closed with required gates and zero receipts, because the band-scoped close gate skipped them until W48. Their argv now resolve and pass when run by hand, but no verb re-runs a closed wave's gates and binds the receipts, so the store still cannot show they ran. Add that path and run it over these waves.
B134.resolution: W07 bound command gates to the P32 and P33 close-time waves and re-receipted 44 at their on-main commits; two reds filed as B161 and B162 (evaluation audit A-P34-I01-EVAL)
B134.title: Bind receipts to the P32 waves that closed without running gates

B135.description: Two defects in one path. A close that fails commits its terminal row before its finally block removes the workspace, so a shutdown in that window cancels a cleanup the executor has not started and leaks the workspace. And cleanup calls git worktree remove on directories git does not list, which reported harness_fault on W44 and W20 after real work finished. Clean up before the terminal commit and remove what the attempt made.
B135.resolution: P33-I01-W12 removes a close workspace the way the attempt created it (rmtree for unlisted, git for listed) before the terminal commit (closeout audit A-P33-CLOSEOUT)
B135.title: Remove a close workspace the way the attempt created it

B136.description: W16 added generations/ (generations, selection pointer, epoch marker, cutover journal, restore point) with no commit-policy row. It only exists in declared disposable canaries today, so nothing reds, but the native epoch-2 path in P33 puts it in live trees. The tree holds transient .staging-* directories that must never be committed, so a single committed row for the whole directory is wrong; split the classification.
B136.resolution: P33-I01-W14 classified the epoch-2 generations tree in the commit policy and .gitignore (closeout audit A-P33-CLOSEOUT)
B136.title: Classify the epoch-2 generation tree before the native path lands

B137.description: W48 fixed the daemon close gate only. The CLI direct-write fallback and the readiness pre-flight still narrow a mechanical non-band wave to advisory under the band-scoped quality profile, so a daemonless close of such a wave runs none of its declared gates. Mirror W48 there, or refuse the daemonless close of a gate-bearing wave.
B137.resolution: P33-I01-W10: the daemonless close path and readiness pre-flight key band narrowing on verify_block.enforce like the daemon path (closeout audit A-P33-CLOSEOUT)
B137.title: Run a band-narrowed wave's gates on the daemonless close path

B138.description: Phase audit F4: W44 added Release.adoption and the adopt verb but closed with zero gates and three attested legacy criteria. Its three test files exist and pass (77 tests), so the behaviour is covered, yet nothing at close would have noticed a regression. Attach command gates to the adoption criteria through spec repoint or a follow-up wave.
B138.resolution: P33-I01-W39 gated the release adoption criteria on the test_dev1_adopt* integration tests (closeout audit A-P33-CLOSEOUT)
B138.title: Gate the release adoption path W44 shipped without gates

B139.description: Phase audit F5: the idle surface is 204 against a 204 ceiling. P32 added validation_rule_payload, ambiguity_label, render_state_diagram, run_census (tools-only caller), compact_terminal_task, recover_store_tree, append_correction and apply_transition, and moved build_receipt_probes still idle. Wire each to its producer as the native epoch-2 path lands, drop the rest, and lower the ceiling; never raise it.
B139.title: Wire or drop the eight idle functions P32 added

B140.description: Phase audit F6: .pre-commit-config.yaml excludes the whole ^tests/fixtures/migration/ and ^tests/golden/kernel/migration/ prefixes from detect-secrets. A scan found 79 hits, all digests, SHAs and id-shaped strings, and no credential, but the exclusion is open-ended. Replace it with a baseline entry or an enumerated file list.
B140.resolution: P33-I01-W28 narrowed the migration detect-secrets exclusion to named files (closeout audit A-P33-CLOSEOUT)
B140.title: Narrow the migration fixture secrets exclusion to named files

B141.description: Phase audit F7: skills/audit.py:423, skills/security_review.py:89 and surfaces/cli/commands/evidence_backlog.py:147 still execute gates in process, outside the sandboxed gate child W27 and W40 introduced for the close scorer. Route them through run_gate_out_of_process or document why each is exempt.
B141.resolution: P33-I01-W13 moved the audit, security-review and audit-run gate paths into run_checks_out_of_process (closeout audit A-P33-CLOSEOUT)
B141.title: Move the last in-process gate paths into the sandboxed child

B142.description: AuditorReportBody requires each criterion echoed verbatim, and the model repeatedly appends (deterministic=true), so three schema re-asks fail and the attempt is typed an infrastructure retry. It cost a full auditor round on W17. Either strip a trailing parenthetical before comparing or stop showing the model an annotated criterion.
B142.resolution: P33-I01-W18 strips the deterministic annotation from the auditor's criterion echo before the verbatim check (closeout audit A-P33-CLOSEOUT)
B142.title: Normalise the auditor's criterion echo before the verbatim check

B143.description: Release.adoption shipped in 0.7.0.dev2 without a schema_version bump, which the changelog states as a limitation: a reader pinned to the previous version cannot tell a record written before the field existed from one that was not adopted. Bump the version with a migration note at the next checkpoint.
B143.resolution: P33-I01-W39 versioned the release record tag (release/v2, release/v1 still readable) and corrected the changelog (closeout audit A-P33-CLOSEOUT)
B143.title: Bump the state schema for the Release.adoption field

B144.description: The publication runbook's step 2 is hand-assembled JSON because no verb moves a release record from DRAFT to CANDIDATE, so an approval is only as trustworthy as that document. P33-I01-W01 drives dev2 through this edge, so the verb is needed there.
B144.resolution: P33-I01-W33 added the release candidate verb for the DRAFT to CANDIDATE edge (closeout audit A-P33-CLOSEOUT)
B144.title: Add an operator verb for the release DRAFT to CANDIDATE edge

B145.description: quiesce_volatile_chrome resets app.degraded but leaves the StateBinding probe running; with no daemon its third failed probe flips degraded about a second after mount, so a golden captured on a slow host within that window can show the degraded banner. W47 parked the probe in one feed test; the harness should detach or park the probe during quiesce.
B145.resolution: P33-I01-W16: the pilot harness parks the state-binding daemon probe during quiesce, so no degraded flip lands late (closeout audit A-P33-CLOSEOUT)
B145.title: Stop quiesce leaving the state binder's pending degraded flip

B146.description: The promoted contract metadata uses scale_band for both the environment class and the corpus magnitude, which breaks the one-name-per-concept rule. W20 flagged it rather than renaming mid-wave. Rename one of the two uses and migrate the metadata.
B146.resolution: W07 runbook refreshed MCT-26091101 metadata from the in-code contract (evaluation audit A-P34-I01-EVAL)
B146.title: Split scale_band into its two concepts

B147.description: W01, W20 and W44 closed with file_scopes that no longer match the files their commits touched, and wave update refuses a CLOSED wave, so the record stays wrong. Mirror spec repoint-gates: rewrite file_scopes only, under a fingerprint guard, from the landed commit.
B147.resolution: P33-I01-W19 added eawf spec repoint-scopes, a bounded file-scope repoint on closed waves (closeout audit A-P33-CLOSEOUT)
B147.title: Allow a bounded file-scope repoint on a closed wave

B148.description: Phase audit F9 and F10: W09 CR-01 names the P14-W02 shorthand, but the ambiguous one in the pinned corpus is P14-W01 (the test covers both). W11's hand-built document.json carries invented P03 archived and B003 closed rows with no marker. Correct the text and mark or split the invented rows.
B148.resolution: W07 runbook corrected P32-I01-W09 CR-01 text to the real ambiguous shorthand (evaluation audit A-P34-I01-EVAL)
B148.title: Correct W09's criterion text and mark W11's invented fixture rows

B149.description: state.json is exempt from path-leak-lint and email-leak-lint (_is_state_bookkeeping_path in surfaces/cli/commands/hook.py) and from detect-secrets, yet its free-text fields take arbitrary agent and operator text; that is how the P08 absolute worktree paths went public. Scan only the added lines of the staged diff with the path and email patterns plus targeted token regexes, keep the detect-secrets exclusion, and prove the gate reds on a seeded leak.
B149.resolution: Resolved by P33-I01-W06: a commit-time lint scans only the lines each commit adds to state.json against the shared path, email and token pattern set, keeps the detect-secrets exclusion, and is proven to red on a seeded leak. The row was left open when the wave closed; closed here at the phase closeout audit.
B149.title: Lint the lines each commit adds to state.json for paths and tokens

B150.description: Nothing under kernel/state scrubs wave descriptions, outcomes, criteria text, backlog titles, incident text or close failure details on write; only the agent-report store rejects a body that fails scan_text. Reuse that check on the daemon mutation path so a leak is refused at write time rather than caught at commit time.
B150.resolution: Resolved by P33-I01-W07: the daemon diffs old against new string values on its single-lock and wave-close commits and on the CLI fallback transaction, and refuses a new string matching the shared leak pattern set. The row was left open when the wave closed; closed here at the phase closeout audit.
B150.title: Scrub free text on the daemon's state.json write path

B151.description: waves[*].sessions[*].session_id, runtime_baseline and runtime_latest session ids carry the Claude Code session UUID, the one value that names a local transcript file, and a few session rows carry subprocess_pid. Neither is needed once a session closes; hash the UUID or drop it and the pid at close.
B151.resolution: Resolved by P33-I01-W08: vendor session identifiers are hashed at every daemon entry point through one idempotent helper, and subprocess pids are no longer persisted at all. The row was left open when the wave closed; closed here at the phase closeout audit.
B151.title: Stop persisting vendor session UUIDs and process ids in state

B152.description: test_doctor_mode_snapshot drifted on the macos-26 leg of PR #39 (run 35098441640): the footer heartbeat dot was blank at capture. quiesce_volatile_chrome forces the dot lit with ack() and captures compositor strips with no frame in between, so the pulse phase still leaks into goldens. Pause the heartbeat's interval timer during quiesce and pump one frame, so the dot is lit and cannot re-blank.
B152.resolution: Resolved by P32-I01-W52: the snapshot quiesce now lights the active screen's heartbeat; the filed timer mechanism was never reached because App.query returned the home screen's heartbeat after a mode switch.
B152.title: Freeze the footer heartbeat before a golden capture

B153.description: ConsoleApp has no production construction site: every caller in src/ is test tooling passing load_fixture() and a FakeClock, so the 261-frame console is unreachable. SURF-173 specifies the eawf tui launch flag. The transport is already proven - the projection seam serves reads and keyed patches over the daemon, and the epoch-1 TUI connects through the identical binding. The open design question is what production passes where the fixture goes. Targeted at P34.
B153.resolution: W30 opens the console from eawf tui on epoch-2 trees over the live seam with a guarded quit (evaluation audit A-P34-I01-EVAL)
B153.title: Launch the epoch-2 console from eawf tui on the live projection seam

B154.description: The v0.7 UI packet judged 82 shipped surfaces under src/eawf/surfaces/tui/: 47 carry into console routes, 27 fold into the chassis, 8 delete. None of that disposition is scheduled, so two TUIs coexist and eawf tui still opens the epoch-1 app. Removal is gated on the 47 carry-overs landing first, or function is lost. Targeted at P35, the flag day, alongside the coverage grid reconciling to the route registry.
B154.title: Retire the epoch-1 TUI against the packet carry-over verdict

B155.description: P37 promises to close every idle contract with a producer and a consumer, but tools/idle_contract_gate.py tracks only hand-registered contracts and carries no console reference, so the console being unreachable would never red it. This is why the launcher omission survived a whole phase unnoticed. Register the launcher as a tracked contract, and prefer a rule that reds on any renderer with no production construction site over one more hand-added row.
B155.resolution: W31 adds an idle-contract rule that reds a TUI App subclass with no reachable launcher (evaluation audit A-P34-I01-EVAL)
B155.title: Track the console launcher as an idle contract so the gate can red

B156.description: commit_worktree_state (daemon/methods/state_worktree.py) writes the full state payload and runs refuse_regressed_state and note_state_written but never state_leak_refusal, which every sibling writer runs (methods/state.py:980 and :1305, cli/_mutation.py:224, epoch2_transaction.py:844, planning/apply.py:837). Reachable from eawf wave land, track sync and dispatch pause, so a landed wave carrying a home-anchored path reaches committed state with the gate never consulted.
B156.resolution: W12 added the leak refusal to the worktree, runtime and codex writers and W47 to every remaining state.json writer with a census (evaluation audit A-P34-I01-EVAL)
B156.title: Run the state leak refusal on the worktree and agent state writers

B157.description: Boot recovery finds trees to repair only via live WAL records, but many append_ledger_record sites commit durable mutations with no WAL record and WAL GC unlinks FSYNCED ones after retention. A kill mid-append leaves a tail with no trailing newline, read_ledger_records raises LedgerTornTailError permanently, and recovery never yields a document path for that root so truncate_torn_tail is never called. Epoch-2 canary trees only.
B157.resolution: W14 truncates a torn ledger tail at boot with one journaled repair row (evaluation audit A-P34-I01-EVAL)
B157.title: Truncate a torn ledger tail left by a write that logs no WAL record

B158.description: About twenty append_ledger_record sites across run, run_budget, delivery, delivery_acceptance, native_dispatch, native_retry, semantic_gateway and semantic_handlers commit durable domain mutations with no WAL intent, no canonical_sequence, no domain event and no firehose row, which is the invariant W52 established. A crash after such an append leaves state the firehose-rebuilt projection cannot see.
B158.resolution: W13 routes every native ledger append through the transaction with an AST census (evaluation audit A-P34-I01-EVAL)
B158.title: Commit epoch-2 ledger-only mutations through the seven-step transaction

W26 and W28 were captured under the wall-clock basis (measure v1), which counted the operator asleep at a permission prompt as agent runtime and inflated them roughly fourfold. W35 and W36 both recorded 0.3769 EU / 3.10 USD and W39 through W42 all recorded 0.0419 EU: one session's runtime handed whole to every wave that shared it (fixed in W46, which cannot retro-split a closed row). alternatives: Set odr_blocking to false and keep the gate advisory (rejected: it lowers a gate the repo deliberately armed and would have meant editing the test that pins the opt-in to match a config change rather than the reverse)

D-I25-ODR-DRAIN.rationale: This supersedes D-ODR-ADVISORY which rested on a false premise. That decision claimed the odr_blocking flag had been inert since it was written because the profile verify-block merge dropped it. It had not: the flag reaches the close path through the repo-config overlay and not through the profile merge, so it has been armed since P30-I23-W25 when the repo opted in after draining the I20 and I21 legacy corpus. The P30-I25-W48 merge repair recovered only PROFILE-declared fields which no shipped profile sets. Verified by running the pre-W48 loader against the pre-flip config: odr_blocking still resolved to true. What actually happened is that the repair-burst waves of P30-I25 were authored with legacy-string criteria under criteria-floor waivers so the iter reintroduced 214 untyped required criteria and its Oracle-Determinism-Ratio was 0.0 against the 0.8 floor. The honest remedy is the one the repo already uses: eawf spec convert-legacy P30-I25 typed all 214 rows with a falsifying criterion_in_diff gate and zero refusals so the iter closes with the gate ARMED AND SATISFIED rather than lowered. The config keeps odr_blocking true. A separate finding stands on its own: P30-I24 closed with an ODR of 0.000 while the gate was armed which means that close went around it; backlog B108 carries it.
D-I25-ODR-DRAIN.title: Drain the I25 criteria rather than lower the ODR gate

alternatives: Pre-flight the jury/LLM tier outside the lock too (rejected: requires state re-apply machinery, deferred to P31)
D-LOCK-SPLIT.rationale: Verify-then-commit split: the deterministic tier + floor pack pre-flight run OUTSIDE the state lock; the jury/LLM tier stays UNDER the lock but wall-clock-bounded. The jury tier mutates state in-memory and appends session events, so pre-flighting it needs re-apply machinery deferred to P31 verifier maturation. Splitting only the deterministic tier removes the long-hold close deadlock class (5 wedge episodes on 2026-07-01).
D-LOCK-SPLIT.title: Split wave close: deterministic pre-flight outside the state lock

alternatives: Leave odr_blocking true and drain the criteria now (rejected: 214 required criteria in this iter alone and every future iter close blocked until its own are typed, which turns a repair iter into a phase-sized campaign)
Leave odr_blocking true and add a typed sub-floor waiver on the iter (rejected: new bypass mechanism authored inside the iter whose purpose was to stop shipping half-wired contracts)
D-ODR-ADVISORY.rationale: The Oracle-Determinism-Ratio scores what fraction of a scope's required criteria are falsified by a reproducible automated oracle (tiers T1 through T5) rather than by a judgment oracle (an approval or a jury reading prose). This repo scores 0.0: every required criterion is a grandfathered legacy string with no oracle tier, so every close rests on someone reading prose. The repo config set verify.odr_blocking to true, but the field was silently dropped by the profile verify-block merge and so gated nothing from the day it was written; P30-I25-W48 fixed the merge and the flag became live, at which point iter close began refusing every iter in the repo. The precondition the field's own contract states is that a profile opts in only after its legacy sub-floor criteria have been drained, and 0 of 214 required criteria in this iter are drained. Setting the flag to false records what the system has actually done since the flag shipped rather than asserting a policy the repo cannot satisfy. The gate re-arms when criteria carry deterministic oracle tiers; backlog item B-ODR-DRAIN carries that campaign. This is a policy statement about an unmet precondition and not a weakening of verification: the close-time auditor, the criteria floor, and the zero-runtime gate are all unaffected.
D-ODR-ADVISORY.title: Keep the ODR gate advisory until the legacy criteria are typed

alternatives: Key the pardon on the counters as W52 CR-02 asked (rejected: it silently pardons a capture path that is alive but frozen which is the exact failure the gate exists to catch)
Drop the pardon entirely and require a waiver for every re-originated wave (rejected: waiver fatigue degrades the signal that makes a waiver worth reading)
D-RESET-PARDON-STRICT.rationale: W52 was authored with a criterion asking that the reset pardon key on whether a capture reported new counters rather than on when it arrived so that a no-op capture cannot strand a re-originated wave. Implementing it as written would weaken the gate and the criterion is therefore superseded. Two states are byte-identical in state.json: an honest reset followed by a capture that measured nothing and a capture path that is alive but reporting a frozen snapshot. Both show the same counters and a later captured_at. A rule that pardons on frozen counters closes the second case in silence which is the original defect of this entire iter where every wave recorded zero effort units for months and nobody noticed. A rule that refuses it costs an explicit no-runtime waiver which is recorded on the wave and visible in review. Silence is the failure this iter exists to eliminate and a waiver is not silence so the strict clock-based rule stands. The wave is not stranded either way because the re-origin guarantees it stays measurable going forward and a later capture that measures something closes it without any waiver at all.
D-RESET-PARDON-STRICT.title: Keep the reset pardon strict and pay for it with a visible waiver

alternatives: Reopen W43 and edit its criteria (rejected: reopening a closed wave to rewrite the contract it was judged against destroys the audit trail that caught the gap)
D-W43-CRITERIA-SUPERSEDED.rationale: P30-I25-W43 shipped two criteria that the delivered code deliberately does not satisfy and the wave is CLOSED so its criteria are immutable. CR-02 promised that the turn still in flight falls back to its row span. The implementation dropped the fallback on purpose: spanning the in-flight turn charges that turn's approval stalls back into the measure and makes the duration DROP when Claude's smaller figure lands which reads as a counter reset and re-origins the wave. It reports zero for an unmeasured turn rather than a guess and the turn is counted at the next capture. CR-03 promised that rows are ordered by timestamp before being grouped into turns. There is no sorting and no grouping because the measure no longer derives turn spans at all; it sums the turn_duration rows Claude writes and a sum is order-independent so the goal holds vacuously. Both departures are improvements on the criteria as written and both were verified by audit 4. This decision records the supersession so a reader comparing the wave contract to the code finds the reason in state rather than concluding the wave under-delivered. The duration ceiling that CR-04 promised was genuinely absent and is repaired by W49 rather than superseded here.
D-W43-CRITERIA-SUPERSEDED.title: Record that the delivered turn measure supersedes two of W43's criteria

alternatives: Keep the de-scope and ship Windows as known-broken (rejected: the transport now passes on a real host, so the de-scope would itself become the false claim)
Cut Windows from v0.6.0 (rejected: it works; removing a working platform to avoid revisiting a decision is backwards)
D-WINDOWS-REALHOST.rationale: D-WINDOWS-DESCOPE deferred Windows because the win32 SID-verify path had never run a real win32 round-trip. The first real run proved the suspicion: the transport shipped six defects, each a call that could not have succeeded once. ImpersonateNamedPipeClient and EqualSid were invoked through modules that do not define them, so the peer-SID check raised AttributeError on every verified connection and the worker closed the pipe; because the daemon's own ping is SID-verified, cold start could never complete. The readiness probe truth-tested a pywin32 call that returns None on success, so it reported every healthy pipe as unready. The listener returned from start before binding the first pipe instance. stop left subscription feeds on the bus. A design test asserted a win32 BOOL is the False singleton. With those fixed the win32 set passes on a real Windows host (65 passed, 4 skipped), so the de-scope premise no longer holds. This row also supersedes D-WINDOWS-VALIDATED, a placeholder a probe command created in error.
D-WINDOWS-REALHOST.title: Windows real-host validation discharged; win32 transport passes

alternatives: verify-before-read (rejected: makes ImpersonateNamedPipeClient unreliable, weakening the second gate)
sub-chunk pre-verify read (deferred: adds a reassembly seam for no change to the bounded-discarded-behind-a-DACL threat surface)
D-WINPIPE-01.rationale: The Windows named-pipe transport reads one bounded 64KB chunk before the post-connect SID verify because ImpersonateNamedPipeClient requires a prior read to establish the client security context. The owner-only pipe DACL is the primary gate (the kernel refuses a non-owner CreateFile before any read), so the pre-verify read is reachable only by a process the kernel already attributes to the owning user; the bytes are bounded and discarded on rejection, nothing is parsed or dispatched pre-verify. Accept the residual rather than reorder (which makes the SID verify unreliable).
D-WINPIPE-01.title: Accept one bounded 64KB pre-verify pipe read; DACL is the gate

alternatives: Keep GitHub rebase merge and auto-repin after every merge
Treat the trailer as identity and the stored SHA as an optional cache
D66.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-09-23. GitHub rebase merge re-creates every commit with a new committer, so every wave pin goes stale at merge and post-merge CI re-tests an already tested tree. From P34 a phase lands by rebasing onto main locally, running CI on that exact SHA and pushing fast-forward to main, so the PR closes as merged with unchanged SHAs. Fallback when SHAs are rewritten anyway: a post-merge repin resolves each Eawf-Wave trailer on first-parent main, disambiguated by git patch-id. A commit may carry several Eawf-Wave trailers (one commit per Batch); the lint instead refuses a rewrite or squash that drops a wave's trailer from main. Pre-merge refs are archived under refs/eawf/archive/<phase>/ before any branch prune. The ship-process rule's merge-with-rebase line is rewritten accordingly.
D66.title: Land phases by fast-forward and repin rewritten pins by trailer
